A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Z-Erase research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-I. Both have 28 pages; appendix pages 12-28 have identical text and rendered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-erasure experiments, adversarial evaluations, ablations and a 30-participant user study in Section 5, with additional results and visual analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Z-Image Turbo comparisons, user-study outcomes and HunyuanImage-3.0 experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same LoRA updates restricted to text tokens, erasure and preservation objectives, and adaptive Lagrangian updates. Multi-concept LoRA averaging in Appendix F is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same I2P, MS-COCO, celebrity, entity, artistic-style and abstraction evaluations, along with adversarial prompts, multi-concept scenarios and human evaluation. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. For example, Table 4 retains DiT-Localization, EraseAnything and Token-Zeroing, while Appendix Table 10 retains DiT-Localization and EraseAnything.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain identical, including the nine-step Euler sampler, 1,000 AdamW training steps, detection thresholds, 50/50 celebrity split and 30-participant user study. Metrics and appendix protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both contain the same loss ablations in Table 5, hyperparameter analyses in Figure 8, adversarial tests in Table 4, and qualitative configuration and preservation analyses in Appendix G. No analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Seed and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Both describe matched seeds for user-study images; neither adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings and qualitative examples match throughout. For example, Table 1 reports 161 nudity detections, FID 26.46 and CLIP 31.25 for Z-Erase in both versions; appendix results are identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, dual derivations and preservation bound in Appendix B, and assumptions and convergence proofs in Appendix C are unchanged. Equation movement across pages does not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty, generation-stability, erasure-preservation and Pareto-convergence claims. The added code-availability sentence does not change the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of architectural coupling, baseline failure modes and preservation trade-offs remain unchanged. Appendix H retains the computational-cost limitation: approximately 35 minutes per concept versus 20 minutes for naive fine-tuning on one H20 GPU.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and the nxjiang-jnx/Z-Erase repository address to the abstract; v1 provides no such pointer. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and timing disclosures are unchanged. Repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and positioning relative to earlier architectures and erasure methods are unchanged. Conference-publication information added to the first page does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 expands affiliations, changes corresponding-author information, replaces preprint boilerplate with conference information, and adds a funding acknowledgment and code sentence. Research prose and scientific section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Abstract styling, first-page spacing and footnotes change, causing main-text and reference reflow around existing displays. Figures, tables and captions retain their content and design; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer modestly improves code discoverability for readers seeking to reproduce the work. Scientific methods, evidence, proofs and limitations remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited to access information and editorial disclosure; the PDFs do not establish repository completeness or usability.
